clue.text: Such destructive behaviour is wicked

definitions.meaning: breaking things to pieces violently, the act of a vandal
slang for excellent or terrific, as in a wicked party

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: wrecking things is this behaviour, and the word is British slang praise meaning terrific.

clue.text: Raised seating area in island's old cinema

indicators.note: the reversed seating word sits inside the island's name

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the pit is the seating area in front of a theatre stage
ex means former or old

explanation.surface: An old picture house on a Scottish island had a tiered seating area.
explanation.walkthrough: In a theatre the pit is the floor-level seating; in a down clue 'Raised' reads it from the bottom up. Mull is a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A complex with several screens is a type of cinema; the word is a common name for one.

clue.text: Amphetamine dearer than before? Make rate even higher

parts.note: speed is street slang for amphetamine
prices that are up have risen

explanation.surface: A drug user notes that amphetamine has gone up in price.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate is to raise a rate further, the phrasal verb for going faster.

clue.text: This piece of land no longer available for rent, apparently

definitions.text: This piece of land no longer available for rent, apparently

parts.words: This piece of land no longer available for rent, apparently
parts.note: a small isle read as two words says a property ..., so no longer up for rent

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a piece of land, and split in two the word announces a property is taken.

clue.text: Information, say, picked up by first of narks

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say

indicators.note: the opening letter of narks is taken

explanation.surface: A police informer, a nark, passes on information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' is a reversal only because this is a down entry, read from the bottom. A nark is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British slang for information, short for general information.

clue.text: Closely examine crumbling arches

indicators.note: crumbling stonework falls apart, so the letters of arches are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inspector looks closely at some crumbling arches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' makes SEARCH from the letters of ARCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To search something is to examine it thoroughly, a close synonym.

clue.text: Separated on a trip

definitions.meaning: set apart with gaps between, like evenly distributed chairs
under the influence of a hallucinogenic drug, dazed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both set at intervals and dazed as if drugged, two common senses.

clue.text: Won't I give support to a region of Ghana?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: shan't I is an old-fashioned way to say won't I

explanation.surface: A question about whether one will back a region of Ghana.
explanation.walkthrough: SHANTI ('shan't I') sits below A, holding it up as 'give support to' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashanti is a historical kingdom and present administrative region in Ghana, the home of the Ashanti people.

clue.text: Fellow socialist disheartened

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
red is a common label for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A fellow left-winger was feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' looks like sad, but here it means literally having had its heart removed, as with an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is cored has had its centre taken out, a literal reading of losing its heart.

clue.text: Colluded regularly, making contribution to crossword

indicators.note: taking every other letter at regular intervals from colluded

explanation.surface: Solvers conspired over a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of Colluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Each prompt in a crossword is one of its clues, so it contributes to the puzzle.

clue.text: Course includes bread with Irish cheese

indicators.note: the course word contains the other two pieces

parts.note: a lane is a course on a running track or in a pool
bread is slang for money, cash

explanation.surface: A meal course of bread with an Irish cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is old slang for money. The answer is a crumbly cheese named after the English county of Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a crumbly English cheese named for its county of origin.

clue.text: Boyfriend living in sin, in good place at last — here?

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good in crossword convention

indicators.note: the boyfriend lives inside the sin word

parts.note: to err is to sin
a date is a romantic partner one is going out with

indicators.note: the final letter of place is taken

explanation.surface: A boyfriend cohabiting unmarried finally finds a good place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living in' puts the boyfriend inside the sin after its first letter, not simply alongside it. The question mark marks 'here' as a definition by example: the place one is living.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secondary residence is where one stays, so a place one might call here.

clue.text: Rocket taking traveller over highest point

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a rep is a travelling salesman
the roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: A rocket carries a traveller above the top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' is British slang for a severe telling-off, not a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is a severe scolding in British slang, as is a reproof.

clue.text: Artist's model given reminder to remove last bit of clothing

indicators.note: the reminder word loses a letter that is taken away

parts.note: a nudge is a prompt or reminder

indicators.note: the final letter of clothing is taken

explanation.surface: An artist's model is reminded to take off the final item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove' takes G, the last letter of clothing, out of NUDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Life models often pose unclothed, so the answer fits an artist's model.

clue.text: Class likely to face reprimand? Nonsense

indicators.note: the first pieces are set before the reprimand word

parts.note: cl is an abbreviation for class
apt means likely or inclined
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A class that tends to get told off is accused of talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious rubbish, a synonym for empty talk.

clue.text: Dog always lags behind on short run

indicators.note: the always word follows the other pieces

parts.note: re means on or about

indicators.note: the run word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a run is a short journey or trip
ever means always

explanation.surface: A dog that is always slow on a short run.
explanation.walkthrough: A run can mean a short journey, as in a run to the shops; 'short' cuts its last letter, and 'lags behind' sends the always word to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a breed of gun dog trained to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Love poem I've briefly written, going round Spanish city

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: turning round reverses the poem and the shortened I've together

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: the word I've is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A love poem written about a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts I've to IV; 'going round' turns ODE and IV into VIEDO, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias in northern Spain.

clue.text: Phone round? Caller has no time for conversations

parts.note: to dial is to phone
a round shape is an O

indicators.note: the caller word is missing a letter

parts.note: a guest is someone who calls round, a visitor

explanation.surface: Someone phones round, but the caller has no time to chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes T out of GUEST, leaving GUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialogues are exchanges between two or more speakers, so conversations.

clue.text: Leave out part of speech that's not right

indicators.note: the extract word is without one letter

parts.note: an excerpt is a part taken from a speech or text

explanation.surface: A grammarian omits a part of speech that is incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of speech' suggests noun or verb, but means an extract from a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To except is to exclude or omit, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Competitor in event ran tirelessly

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of words event ran tirelessly

explanation.surface: A competitor in an event ran without tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across evENT RAN Tirelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who enters a contest, so a competitor.

clue.text: Understand how to become popular

definitions.meaning: to spread and gain favour, as a fashion does

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to grasp an idea and for a craze to spread.

clue.text: Bird caught near Balmoral?

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a balmoral is a flat Scottish bonnet, a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A bird captured close to the royal castle in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral looks like the royal castle in Scotland but here is a Scottish bonnet; the question mark flags it as an example of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The chat is a small songbird, such as the stonechat or whinchat.

clue.text: Orchestra in concert venue close to Knightsbridge

parts.note: a large room or building where concerts are given

indicators.note: the closing letter of Knightsbridge is taken

explanation.surface: An orchestra plays in a concert hall near Knightsbridge in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Knightsbridge is a London district, home of the Royal Albert Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallé is a Manchester symphony orchestra founded by Charles Hallé.

clue.text: Violation of home: father initiates legal proceedings

indicators.note: the father abbreviation comes at the start of the proceedings word

parts.note: in means at home
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A father takes legal action over a violation of his home.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a breach of a rule or law, so a violation.

clue.text: An experienced player enters stage

indicators.note: the player word goes into the word an

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a seasoned player

explanation.surface: A seasoned actor steps onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The apron is the part of a stage in front of the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the part of a theatre stage projecting beyond the proscenium.

clue.text: Bill wears overalls, working in country abroad

indicators.note: the overalls letters are worn around the bill word
working means reworked, so the letters of overalls are rearranged

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A man named Bill dons overalls to work abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of overalls to ELSALVOR, which 'wears' around Bill's abbreviation. Bill is a poster here, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: El Salvador is a republic in Central America, a foreign country.

clue.text: Swimmer's stroke

definitions.meaning: a small flatfish, so a swimmer; 's is is

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small flatfish and also a light quick touch.

clue.text: For example, queen's not on time

indicators.note: the queen word is without the letters of on

parts.note: in card games a queen is one of the honours
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch is late, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are honour cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time, sixty minutes.

clue.text: One disturbs game birds initially by shaking a tree

indicators.note: the opening letter of birds is taken
shaking moves things about, so the letters of a tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone startles game birds by shaking a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' makes EATER from A TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beater flushes game birds out of cover for the guns on a shoot.

clue.text: One managing to hide figure's skeletal appearance

indicators.note: the manager word conceals the figure inside it

parts.note: a boss is someone in charge
nine is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A manager hides a figure of skeletal thinness.
explanation.definitionFit: A bony look is thinness that shows the skeleton, a gaunt appearance.
